```{r data}
# ---- Load the raw UCI file (';' separated; a ',' copy from Kaggle also works)
data_path <- "student-mat.csv"
sep <- if (grepl(";", readLines(data_path, n = 1))) ";" else ","
d <- read.csv(data_path, sep = sep, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 395, ncol(d) == 33, !anyNA(d))

d$internet    <- factor(d$internet, levels = c("no", "yes"),
                        labels = c("No internet", "Internet"))
d$school      <- factor(d$school)
d$studytime_n <- d$studytime
d$studytime   <- factor(d$studytime, levels = 1:4,
                        labels = c("<2 h", "2-5 h", "5-10 h", ">10 h"))
```

```{r helpers}
# ---- APA formatting helpers
f2    <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)
nl    <- function(x, d = 2) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)) # no leading zero
pcell <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", nl(p, 3))
pfmt  <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", paste("=", nl(p, 3)))
pct   <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
sig   <- function(p) ifelse(p < .05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")
d_lab   <- function(x) { x <- abs(x); ifelse(x < .2, "negligible", ifelse(x < .5, "small", ifelse(x < .8, "medium", "large"))) }
eta_lab <- function(x) ifelse(x < .01, "very small", ifelse(x < .06, "small", ifelse(x < .14, "medium", "large")))
r_lab   <- function(x) { x <- abs(x); ifelse(x < .1, "negligible", ifelse(x < .3, "small", ifelse(x < .5, "medium", "large"))) }
v_lab   <- function(x) ifelse(x < .1, "negligible", ifelse(x < .3, "small", ifelse(x < .5, "medium", "large")))

# Levene's test, median-centred (same as car::leveneTest default)
levene_med <- function(y, g) {
  g <- factor(g)
  z <- abs(y - ave(y, g, FUN = median))
  a <- anova(lm(z ~ g))
  c(F = a$`F value`[1], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}
```

```{r compute}
# ---- 1. Welch t-test
tt  <- t.test(G3 ~ internet, data = d)
g3  <- split(d$G3, d$internet)
gn  <- sapply(g3, length); gm <- sapply(g3, mean); gs <- sapply(g3, sd)
sp  <- sqrt(((gn[1] - 1) * gs[1]^2 + (gn[2] - 1) * gs[2]^2) / (sum(gn) - 2))
d_t <- unname((gm[2] - gm[1]) / sp)                 # Internet minus No internet
lev_t <- levene_med(d$G3, d$internet)
sh_t  <- sapply(g3, function(x) shapiro.test(x)$p.value)

# ---- 2. One-way ANOVA + Tukey
fit  <- aov(G3 ~ studytime, data = d)
a    <- summary(fit)[[1]]
F_a  <- a$`F value`[1]; df1 <- a$Df[1]; df2 <- a$Df[2]; p_a <- a$`Pr(>F)`[1]
eta2 <- a$`Sum Sq`[1] / sum(a$`Sum Sq`)
tuk  <- TukeyHSD(fit)$studytime
lev_a <- levene_med(d$G3, d$studytime)
sh_a  <- shapiro.test(residuals(fit))$p.value

# ---- 3. Pearson correlation
ct <- cor.test(d$G1, d$G3)

# ---- 4. Multiple regression
m   <- lm(G3 ~ studytime_n + absences + failures, data = d)
sm  <- summary(m)
ms  <- lm(scale(G3) ~ scale(studytime_n) + scale(absences) + scale(failures), data = d)
ci  <- confint(m)
fs  <- sm$fstatistic
p_m <- pf(fs[1], fs[2], fs[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
sh_m <- shapiro.test(residuals(m))$p.value
cook <- max(cooks.distance(m))

# ---- 5. Chi-square (school x internet)
tab <- table(school = d$school, internet = d$internet)
cs  <- chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)
V   <- sqrt(unname(cs$statistic) / (sum(tab) * min(dim(tab) - 1)))
```

# Summary

This report analyses the public *Student Performance* dataset (Cortez & Silva, 2008; Cortez, 2008): `r nrow(d)` secondary-school mathematics students from two Portuguese schools. Five analyses are shown, each with an assumption check, an APA-style table or figure, and a plain-language interpretation. Final grade (G3) is scored 0 to 20.

```{r summary-table}
sumtab <- data.frame(
  Analysis = c("Welch t-test: G3 by internet access",
               "One-way ANOVA: G3 by study time",
               "Pearson correlation: G1 and G3",
               "Multiple regression: G3 on study time, absences, failures",
               "Chi-square: school by internet access"),
  Statistic = c(sprintf("t(%s) = %s", f2(tt$parameter), f2(tt$statistic)),
                sprintf("F(%d, %d) = %s", df1, df2, f2(F_a)),
                sprintf("r(%d) = %s", ct$parameter, nl(ct$estimate)),
                sprintf("F(%d, %d) = %s", fs[2], fs[3], f2(fs[1])),
                sprintf("chi2(%d) = %s", cs$parameter, f2(cs$statistic))),
  p = c(pcell(tt$p.value), pcell(p_a), pcell(ct$p.value), pcell(p_m), pcell(cs$p.value)),
  `Effect size` = c(sprintf("d = %s (%s)", f2(abs(d_t)), d_lab(d_t)),
                    sprintf("eta2 = %s (%s)", nl(eta2, 3), eta_lab(eta2)),
                    sprintf("r = %s (%s)", nl(ct$estimate), r_lab(ct$estimate)),
                    sprintf("R2 = %s", nl(sm$r.squared, 3)),
                    sprintf("V = %s (%s)", nl(V), v_lab(V))),
  Result = c(ifelse(tt$p.value < .05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
             ifelse(p_a < .05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
             ifelse(ct$p.value < .05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
             ifelse(p_m < .05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
             ifelse(cs$p.value < .05, "Significant", "Not significant")),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(sumtab, align = "lllll")
```

*Note.* Effect-size labels follow Cohen's conventions. $\chi^2$ is written chi2, $\eta^2$ is eta2 and $R^2$ is R2 in this table only.

# Data and descriptive statistics

The file `student-mat.csv` contains 33 variables for `r nrow(d)` students with no missing values. Variables used here are the first-, second- and final-period grades (G1, G2, G3), weekly study time (1 = less than 2 h, 2 = 2 to 5 h, 3 = 5 to 10 h, 4 = more than 10 h), number of past class failures, number of school absences, school (GP or MS) and home internet access.

**Table 1**

*Descriptive Statistics for Study Variables (N = `r nrow(d)`)*

```{r desc-table}
dv  <- c("G1", "G2", "G3", "studytime_n", "failures", "absences")
lab <- c("First-period grade (G1)", "Second-period grade (G2)", "Final grade (G3)",
         "Weekly study time (1-4)", "Past class failures", "Absences")
desc <- data.frame(
  Variable = lab,
  M   = unname(sapply(d[dv], function(x) f2(mean(x)))),
  SD  = unname(sapply(d[dv], function(x) f2(sd(x)))),
  Min = unname(sapply(d[dv], min)),
  Max = unname(sapply(d[dv], max))
)
knitr::kable(desc, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

# Welch independent-samples t-test

**Research question.** Do students with home internet access have different final grades from students without it?

**Assumptions.** Welch's test does not assume equal variances. Levene's test (median-centred) agreed that variances were similar, *F* = `r f2(lev_t["F"])`, *p* `r pfmt(lev_t["p"])`. Shapiro-Wilk tests showed departures from normality in both groups (largest *p* `r pfmt(max(sh_t))`), which is expected for bounded integer grades. With `r gn[1]` and `r gn[2]` students per group, the t-test is fairly robust, but the result should be read with care.

**Table 2**

*Final Grade (G3) by Home Internet Access*

```{r t-table}
ttab <- data.frame(
  Group = names(gm),
  n  = as.integer(gn),
  M  = f2(gm),
  SD = f2(gs)
)
knitr::kable(ttab, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

*Note.* Welch test, difference (No internet minus Internet) = `r f2(diff(rev(gm)))`, 95% CI [`r f2(tt$conf.int[1])`, `r f2(tt$conf.int[2])`], *t*(`r f2(tt$parameter)`) = `r f2(tt$statistic)`, *p* `r pfmt(tt$p.value)`, Cohen's *d* = `r f2(abs(d_t))`.

**Figure 1**

*Final Grade by Home Internet Access*

```{r fig-t}
ggplot(d, aes(internet, G3)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .45, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey90", colour = "grey20") +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = 0, alpha = .35, size = 1.2, colour = "grey30") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 3, fill = "white") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Final grade (G3, 0-20)")
```

*Note.* Diamonds show group means; boxes show medians and quartiles.

**Interpretation.** Students with internet access (*M* = `r f2(gm[2])`, *SD* = `r f2(gs[2])`) scored `r f2(gm[2] - gm[1])` points higher than students without it (*M* = `r f2(gm[1])`, *SD* = `r f2(gs[1])`). The difference was `r sig(tt$p.value)`, *t*(`r f2(tt$parameter)`) = `r f2(tt$statistic)`, *p* `r pfmt(tt$p.value)`, with a `r d_lab(d_t)` effect (*d* = `r f2(abs(d_t))`). `r if (abs(tt$p.value - .05) < .005) paste0("The p value (", sprintf("%.4f", tt$p.value), " before rounding) sits right on the .05 boundary, and the confidence interval almost touches zero, so this is weak evidence and should be replicated before being relied on.") else ""` Because the data are observational, internet access may stand in for family resources and should not be read as a cause of higher grades.

# One-way ANOVA

**Research question.** Do final grades differ across the four weekly study-time levels?

**Assumptions.** Levene's test indicated `r ifelse(lev_a["p"] < .05, "unequal", "similar")` variances across groups, *F*(`r df1`, `r df2`) = `r f2(lev_a["F"])`, *p* `r pfmt(lev_a["p"])`. Residuals departed from normality (Shapiro-Wilk *p* `r pfmt(sh_a)`), which is common for grade data; the groups are unequal in size (`r paste(table(d$studytime), collapse = ", ")`), so conclusions are tentative.

**Table 3**

*Final Grade (G3) by Weekly Study Time*

```{r anova-table}
s2 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$studytime), function(x) {
  n <- nrow(x); mu <- mean(x$G3); se <- sd(x$G3) / sqrt(n)
  data.frame(studytime = x$studytime[1], n = n, M = mu, SD = sd(x$G3),
             lo = mu - qt(.975, n - 1) * se, hi = mu + qt(.975, n - 1) * se)
}))
atab <- data.frame(
  `Study time` = as.character(s2$studytime), n = s2$n,
  M = f2(s2$M), SD = f2(s2$SD),
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%s, %s]", f2(s2$lo), f2(s2$hi)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(atab, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

*Note.* One-way ANOVA: *F*(`r df1`, `r df2`) = `r f2(F_a)`, *p* `r pfmt(p_a)`, $\eta^2$ = `r nl(eta2, 3)`.

**Table 4**

*Tukey HSD Pairwise Comparisons of Study-Time Groups*

```{r tukey-table}
ttab2 <- data.frame(
  Comparison = rownames(tuk),
  `Mean difference` = f2(tuk[, "diff"]),
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%s, %s]", f2(tuk[, "lwr"]), f2(tuk[, "upr"])),
  `p (adjusted)` = pcell(tuk[, "p adj"]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(ttab2, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

**Figure 2**

*Mean Final Grade by Weekly Study Time*

```{r fig-anova}
ggplot(s2, aes(studytime, M, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = .12, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "grey10") +
  labs(x = "Weekly study time", y = "Mean final grade (G3)")
```

*Note.* Error bars show 95% confidence intervals.

**Interpretation.** Mean grades rose from `r f2(s2$M[1])` (less than 2 h) to `r f2(max(s2$M))` at the highest-scoring study-time group, but the overall effect of study time was `r sig(p_a)`, *F*(`r df1`, `r df2`) = `r f2(F_a)`, *p* `r pfmt(p_a)`, $\eta^2$ = `r nl(eta2, 3)` (`r eta_lab(eta2)` effect). `r if (all(tuk[, "p adj"] >= .05)) "No pairwise comparison reached significance after Tukey adjustment." else "At least one pairwise comparison was significant after Tukey adjustment (Table 4)."` Self-reported study time explains very little of the variation in final grade in this sample.

# Pearson correlation

**Research question.** How strongly are first-period (G1) and final (G3) grades related?

**Figure 3**

*First-Period Grade and Final Grade*

```{r fig-cor}
ggplot(d, aes(G1, G3)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .25, height = .25, alpha = .4, size = 1.4, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black", fill = "grey70") +
  labs(x = "First-period grade (G1)", y = "Final grade (G3)")
```

*Note.* Points are jittered slightly because grades are whole numbers. The line is the least-squares fit with a 95% confidence band.

**Result.** G1 and G3 were strongly and positively correlated, *r*(`r ct$parameter`) = `r nl(ct$estimate)`, 95% CI [`r nl(ct$conf.int[1])`, `r nl(ct$conf.int[2])`], *p* `r pfmt(ct$p.value)`. G1 shares about `r pct(ct$estimate^2)` of its variance with G3 ($r^2$ = `r nl(ct$estimate^2)`). Students who start well tend to finish well, which is useful for early-warning systems but says nothing about why.

# Multiple linear regression

**Research question.** How well do weekly study time, absences and past failures together predict the final grade?

**Table 5**

*Regression of Final Grade (G3) on Study Time, Absences and Past Failures*

```{r reg-table}
labs_m <- c("Intercept", "Weekly study time (1-4)", "Absences", "Past class failures")
cf <- sm$coefficients
rtab <- data.frame(
  Predictor = labs_m,
  B   = f2(cf[, 1]),
  SE  = f2(cf[, 2]),
  `Std. beta` = c("", f2(coef(ms)[-1])),
  t   = f2(cf[, 3]),
  p   = pcell(cf[, 4]),
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%s, %s]", f2(ci[, 1]), f2(ci[, 2])),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(rtab, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

*Note.* *N* = `r nobs(m)`. $R^2$ = `r nl(sm$r.squared, 3)`, adjusted $R^2$ = `r nl(sm$adj.r.squared, 3)`, *F*(`r fs[2]`, `r fs[3]`) = `r f2(fs[1])`, *p* `r pfmt(p_m)`. Residual *SE* = `r f2(sm$sigma)`.

**Assumptions.** The largest Cook's distance was `r f2(cook, 3)` (well below 1), so no single student drives the result. Residuals deviated from normality (Shapiro-Wilk *p* `r pfmt(sh_m)`, see Figure 4), so standard errors and *p* values should be read as approximate.

**Figure 4**

*Normal Q-Q Plot of Regression Residuals*

```{r fig-qq}
ggplot(data.frame(res = residuals(m)), aes(sample = res)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = .5, colour = "grey30") + stat_qq_line(colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles")
```

**Interpretation.** The model was `r sig(p_m)` and explained `r pct(sm$r.squared)` of the variance in final grade, *F*(`r fs[2]`, `r fs[3]`) = `r f2(fs[1])`, *p* `r pfmt(p_m)`. Past failures was the dominant predictor: each additional failure was associated with a drop of `r f2(abs(cf[4, 1]))` grade points (*B* = `r f2(cf[4, 1])`, *p* `r pfmt(cf[4, 4])`, standardised $\beta$ = `r f2(coef(ms)[4])`) after accounting for the other predictors. Study time (*p* `r pfmt(cf[2, 4])`) and absences (*p* `r pfmt(cf[3, 4])`) did not add significant independent prediction.

# Chi-square test of independence

**Research question.** Is school (GP vs. MS) associated with having internet at home?

**Table 6**

*Home Internet Access by School*

```{r chi-table}
rp <- prop.table(tab, 1)
ctab <- data.frame(
  School = rownames(tab),
  `No internet, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%s)", tab[, 1], pct(rp[, 1])),
  `Internet, n (%)`    = sprintf("%d (%s)", tab[, 2], pct(rp[, 2])),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(ctab, align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

*Note.* Percentages are row percentages.

**Figure 5**

*Proportion of Students With Home Internet Access, by School*

```{r fig-chi}
pd <- as.data.frame(rp, responseName = "prop")
ggplot(pd, aes(school, prop, fill = internet)) +
  geom_col(width = .55, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey85", "grey40"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")) +
  labs(x = "School", y = "Share of students")
```

**Result.** All expected counts were at least 5 (smallest = `r f2(min(cs$expected))`), so the chi-square test is appropriate. School and internet access were `r ifelse(cs$p.value < .05, "significantly associated", "not significantly associated")`, $\chi^2$(`r cs$parameter`, *N* = `r sum(tab)`) = `r f2(cs$statistic)`, *p* `r pfmt(cs$p.value)`, Cramér's *V* = `r nl(V)` (`r v_lab(V)` effect). Internet access was reported by `r pct(rp[1, 2])` of students at `r rownames(tab)[1]` and `r pct(rp[2, 2])` at `r rownames(tab)[2]`.

# Limitations

- The data come from two Portuguese schools, so results may not generalise to other countries or years.
- All variables are observational and self-reported. No causal claims are made.
- Grades are bounded whole numbers with zeros, so normality assumptions are only approximately met. Robust or non-parametric checks would be added in a full thesis analysis.
- Five tests were run for demonstration. In a real study, multiple comparisons and a pre-specified analysis plan would be reported.

# Reproducibility

```{r repro, echo=FALSE}
chk <- NULL
gt <- "r-ground-truth.json"
if (file.exists(gt) && requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  j <- jsonlite::fromJSON(gt)
  same <- function(a, b) isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(a), as.numeric(b), tolerance = 1e-6))
  chk <- data.frame(
    Check = c("Welch t", "ANOVA F", "Pearson r", "Regression R2", "Chi-square"),
    `Matches r-ground-truth.json` = c(
      same(tt$statistic, j$t_test$t), same(F_a, j$anova$F),
      same(ct$estimate, j$correlation$r), same(sm$r.squared, j$regression$r_squared),
      same(cs$statistic, j$chi_square$chi2)),
    check.names = FALSE)
}
if (!is.null(chk)) knitr::kable(chk, align = "lc") else cat("(r-ground-truth.json not found in this folder; verification skipped.)")
```

Analysis: `r R.version.string`; ggplot2 `r as.character(packageVersion("ggplot2"))`. All code, the cleaned data file and the verification file are available on request and in the project repository.
